requirement.summary: Clean install, migration, build, API, Worker, Dispatcher, and graceful shutdown use the published roles.
Migrations are repeatable before and after populated runtime operation without changing public state.
Versioned seed import accepts all valid scale and rejects every published defect atomically.
OpenAPI 3.1 describes every public HTTP route, error, header, and outbound ParcelFlow webhook.
Media type, JSON, schema, ID, cursor, key, auth, and not-found failures use stable envelopes with zero side effects.
Catalog, inventory, and Order scalar and cardinality boundaries are enforced without coercion or truncation.
Catalog, inventory, and Order reads combine filters, stable ordering, opaque cursor pagination, and restart continuation.
Admin Warehouse, SKU, and Stock Position mutations preserve resource shape, uniqueness, reservations, and replay.
A V1 multi-line Order atomically chooses the first complete Warehouse, reserves every line, and creates one Fulfillment and Event.
V1 rejects aggregate-only cross-Warehouse capacity with one durable domain conflict and no partial effect.
Workers settle each Fulfillment once into one Shipment and exact Stock Position and Event effects.
Cancellation releases reservations once, replays logically, rejects Shipment, and survives restart.
Webhook headers and semantic JSON preserve Event identity and increasing per-Order sequence.
Order list and detail expose durable line, Fulfillment, Shipment, filter, and ordering semantics.
FINAL deterministically splits only when needed and aggregates group Shipment state from ALLOCATED through PARTIALLY_SHIPPED to SHIPPED.
FINAL preserves singular Fulfillment for one Warehouse, returns null for split, and applies split cancellation and Event rules.
FINAL must use the first complete single Warehouse before considering stable cross-Warehouse splitting.
Concurrent Order creation and onHand updates preserve full-order atomicity and Stock Position conservation.
FINAL split allocation sorts SKU then Warehouse, consumes greedily, and groups each participating Warehouse once.
A client disconnect after an upstream mutation commits replays the original result across instances and restart.
Scoped keys distinguish operations and resources while canonical JSON and Order-line reorder replay semantically.
One hundred same-key requests across two APIs and a process death converge to one Order and one response.
Distinct-key hot Stock Position contention has exact successes and conflicts without oversell, deadlock, or 5xx.
Shipment and cancellation races end in exactly one legal terminal Order and Stock Position outcome.
Competing split Orders commit every Allocation and Fulfillment or none without deadlock or partial inventory.
Concurrent group Shipment and whole-Order cancellation produce either complete cancellation or complete Shipment without mixed groups.
Four Workers drain a public ALLOCATED Order backlog to unique Shipments and exact settlements.
Killing an active Worker while public backlog remains cannot strand an Order or duplicate a business effect.
A complete Worker outage followed by a fresh process resumes every committed pending Fulfillment.
Concurrent Worker completion and Worker restart retain one Shipment and settlement per Fulfillment while draining backlog.
A committed cancellation permanently fences pending single and split Fulfillments from later Shipment.
Cold restarting API, Worker, and Dispatcher retains reads and replay while completing pending Shipment and delivery.
An unknown receiver acknowledgement followed by Dispatcher death retries the same Event identity and semantic body until 2xx.
Two Dispatchers preserve successful per-Order sequence through retry and death while allowing cross-Order progress.
An independent contract oracle validates live success and published error traffic against nontrivial OpenAPI 3.1 schemas.
Production Chromium visible controls browse catalog and inventory, create an Order, observe Shipment, and survive refresh.
Production UI cancellation, async Shipment progress, inventory, history, retry, and navigation reflect durable backend state.
Production UI renders dynamic single and split Fulfillments, partial progress, final Shipment, cancellation, and inventory at both viewports.
Production UI visibly handles loading, empty, capacity and idempotency conflicts, stale restart, offline, permission, and retry.
Primary desktop and mobile flows have keyboard-reachable controls, associated labels, focus, and meaningful status announcements.
Published project gates exercise real PostgreSQL, HTTP, Chromium, multi-process, and SIGKILL seams with meaningful assertions.
Every applicable observable requirement closes from contract through runtime, OpenAPI, UI, and public state or receiver evidence.
A frozen V1 binary creates populated states that FINAL migrates into one compatible Fulfillment without identity or history loss.
Saved V1 success and conflict replays and Event identities remain byte-logical compatible after FINAL migration.
V1 pending Fulfillment and unacknowledged delivery continue once after FINAL upgrade without duplicate identity or settlement.
The exact large dataset and 64-client production query workload meet published p95, throughput, 5xx, and correctness thresholds.
The exact hot inventory production workload meets mutation p95, aggregate and successful mutation throughput, 5xx, and inventory correctness.
Five thousand due Fulfillments and deliveries meet published 60 and 120 second recovery thresholds with complete identity and inventory checks.
Public commands are deterministic and noninteractive, propagate failures, terminate descendants, and leave no secret-bearing or submission artifacts.
